article_content: When I informed my daughter that I would no longer be going to an office daily, she looked thrilled. But her next words surprised me. ‘Does that mean you can pick me up from school in the afternoons?’ My daughter, Lydia, is not seven, but 14. I never expected a teenager to want her mother at the school gates, but Lydia does, just like younger children who rush into their parents' arms. I’ve been picking her up for six weeks since leaving my office job to write at home. When I asked why my presence matters so much, her response was revealing. ‘When I see you, Mum, I know that I’m safe.’ It’s eye-opening to realize that my teenage daughter needs me as much now as she did when she was little. When Lydia was born, I took a year off to bond with her. Going back to work was hard, but now I understand how crucial my presence is during her teenage years. I believe parents should have 'teenternity leave' to support their teenagers, just like maternity leave. In the six weeks I’ve been home, Lydia seems happier and more organized. She eats healthier, does her homework without fuss, and sleeps better. Modern teenagers face immense pressures, especially from social media. They need closer parental guidance now more than ever. Today’s teens are constantly connected, with no escape from peer judgment. This digital world can severely affect their self-esteem. I’ve seen how hard it is for Lydia to come home to an empty house and turn to social media for company. My older daughter had it easier just a decade ago. Now, parents need to be as vigilant with teenagers as with toddlers. Setting boundaries, like a 'no screens after 9pm' rule, can help. Enforcing this means confiscating phones and unplugging the router, but we all sleep better. Teenagers may seem self-sufficient, but they need us just as much as younger children. Paying attention to them, even if they prefer their screens, is crucial. We can’t disconnect from the digital world, but we can ensure they have time to relax. I’m grateful I made this change in my work pattern; it’s made a world of difference for Lydia.

article_content: During the first half of their Premier League match against Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday, Chelsea might have been awarded a penalty. Two notable incidents occurred in the penalty area. First, Chris Smalling appeared to grapple with Branislav Ivanovic, pulling him down. Simultaneously, Marcos Rojo seemed to restrain John Terry in a similar manner. Sportsmail's GRAHAM POLL analyzed referee Phil Dowd's handling of these events. Both Smalling and Rojo seemed to have their opponents in headlocks, which should have been visible to Dowd. Ivanovic's dramatic reaction indicated the severity of the infraction. These incidents were deemed more egregious than a similar one involving Ryan Shawcross the previous week. Dowd's decision to overlook these fouls was seen as a letdown, not only for Chelsea but also for fellow referee Michael Oliver, who had correctly awarded a penalty to Swansea for a similar offense. This oversight reinforced the frustration among neutrals regarding the persistent issue of holding during set pieces. Sky Sports reviewed the incident at halftime, highlighting both Terry and Ivanovic being held. The general consensus was that Dowd's inaction was a significant disappointment, affecting the broader perception of refereeing standards.

article_content: If Louis van Gaal had planned the ideal scenario for his revamped Manchester United team, he couldn't have done better than their win over QPR on Sunday. The match saw a stunning Old Trafford debut for record signing Angel di Maria, Ander Herrera's first goal for the club, and impressive performances from newcomers Daley Blind and Marcos Rojo. This allowed Van Gaal to bring on Radamel Falcao with the team already leading 4-0. The atmosphere at Old Trafford was electric, a stark contrast to the mediocre period under David Moyes and the slow start of Van Gaal's tenure. This victory signaled a significant transformation for the team. Angel di Maria's goal celebration and the frustrations of Robin van Persie highlighted the day's events. One challenge for Van Gaal is integrating his star players, especially Juan Mata, whose role was questioned after his £37m signing. Despite initial doubts, Mata has proven his worth, scoring consistently and linking well with Di Maria, Herrera, and Blind. His performance has been crucial to United's strategy and will remain so even as Michael Carrick and Marouane Fellaini return from injury. However, Robin van Persie's form is a concern. Once a key player, his recent performances have been lackluster. His struggles were evident on Sunday, and with Radamel Falcao's arrival, Van Persie's place in the starting lineup is under threat. Van Gaal has tough decisions ahead, especially with Wayne Rooney as captain and Falcao ready to start. The match also saw former United defender Rio Ferdinand competing against his old teammates, further highlighting the changing dynamics within the club.
